what: Changes in this gene can help some cancers grow, including some lung, brain and breast cancers.
intro.test_report: If a test report mentions EGFR, it is noting a finding about this gene. That note is not a diagnosis, and it is not a decision about treatment.

lines.text: Afatinib (Gilotrif): a pill that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with certain EGFR mutations. Authorised in Europe since 2013.
Amivantamab (Rybrevant): a lab-made antibody. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change. Authorised in Europe since 2021.
Cetuximab (ERBITUX): a drug that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for head and neck cancer. Authorised in Europe since 2004.
Dacomitinib (Vizimpro): a drug that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change.
Datopotamab Deruxtecan: a lab-made antibody linked to a drug. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR mutation. Authorised in Europe since 2025.
Erlotinib (Tarceva): a pill that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change.
Gefitinib (Iressa): a pill. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change. Authorised in Europe since 2009.
Lazertinib (LAZCLUZE): a drug that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change.
Osimertinib (TAGRISSO): a drug that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change.
Panitumumab (Vectibix): a drug that blocks the EGFR signal. Approved for advanced bowel cancer with no KRAS gene change. Authorised in Europe since 2007.
Ramucirumab (CYRAMZA): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R change.
Sunvozertinib (Zegfrovy): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for advanced lung cancer with an EGFR exon 20 insertion.
Mobocertinib (Exkivity): withdrawn from the US market. The FDA withdrew approval in 2024.
